text:
Incident Bot: ALERT: Synthetic canary eu-west-1/edge-prober has crossed error-rate threshold (5m window) -> firing PagerDuty incident PD-INC-202603. Pattern: ~95% 5xx on /v1/healthcheck. Stacktrace snippets attached by prober.
PagerDuty: [PD-INC-202603] Triggered by rule: canary_euw_error_rate_high. Priority: P1. Escalation policy: oncall-sre. Links: https://pagerduty.mock/PD-INC-202603
Kai Chen: acked. I’m on it. Starting triage — pulling probe logs and recent deploys.
Meera Patel: +1 ack. I see a huge spike in duplicate pages in PagerDuty, looks like PD shows 4 active incidents with same alert name. Can someone check dedup keys?
Brendan M: I’m seeing the same — our prober runner restarted 3x in the last 2m in EU-West, each generate a separate PD event. Looks like dedup key uses a transient run_id.
Sara L: That would explain oncall flood. Customers impacted? Any 5xx from production backends or just prober-level failures?
Kai Chen: Quick check — backend service metrics (svc-edge) show normal 2xx rates from real traffic. The failures are internal prober assertion errors when validating TLS cert chains. Sample prober error:
```
2026-03-15T18:07:02Z prober[euw-03]: verify_cert: handshake failed: cert chain truncated
stack: prober/runner.go:212 -> prober/check_tls.go:98
run_id: run_20260315_180702_1
```
Meera Patel: So this is prober TLS validation flapping + prober restart loop causing duplicate PD incidents. Impact to customers: none observed in production traffic so far, but synthetic alerts are noisy and hide real problems.
Brendan M: Root cause hypothesis: recent prober release 2026.03.14 bumped cert validation lib, introduced stricter chain length check and a crash-on-error when cert is malformed. The prober auto-restarts on crash, and dedup logic uses run_id so each restart fires a new PD incident.
Kai Chen: Mitigation plan: 1) Silence PD escalation for PD-INC-202603 to stop paging cascade (short-term). 2) Roll back prober release to previous container image in eu-west prober fleet. 3) Patch dedup key to include a stable probe identifier instead of run_id, and add 30s restart backoff.
Sara L: I can silence the PD incident for 30m. Doing now. Reason: noisy duplicate pages during investigation. :white_check_mark:
PagerDuty: PD-INC-202603 silenced for 30m by Sara L.
Ops Rotation Bot: Handoff notice: Kai Chen is currently primary oncall; next rotation Brendan M in 1h.
Meera Patel: Kai, can you push a canary rollback for euw prober? If container rollback is trivial we should do that to stop crashes.
Kai Chen: On it. Rolling back to sha256:abc123 (previous stable). Command:
```
kubectl set image deployment/prober-euw prober=registry.redwood/prober:sha256-abc123 -n telemetry
```
Kai Chen: Rollout started.
Brendan M: Also creating a temp PD suppression rule to dedupe alerts from that prober group until we fix dedup key.
Meera Patel: Noted. I’ll open a fastfix PR to change dedup key to `probe_name` + `probe_target` (stable) and add a crash count guard so we don't immediately fire again.
Kai Chen: Rollback completed on euw cluster. Pods are coming up, healthchecks green locally. I’m watching error rate on the canary dashboard.
Kai Chen: Error rate dropped from ~94% to 1.2% over 2m. No more new PD incidents. Great.
Meera Patel: I’ve pushed the dedup-key PR to staging (link: https://git.mock/r/redwood/prober/pull/432). Tests added for restart loop dedupe. Requesting urgent review from infra team.
Sara L: FYI I’ve updated the incident description in PagerDuty to note: noisy duplicate pages due to prober restart loop; production traffic unaffected. Also added runbook link.
Incident Bot: NOTE added to thread: runbook/prober-incident-guides#tls-flap
Brendan M: Follow-ups: 1) postmortem to include why the stricter cert validation shipped without a canary on prober fleet; 2) add PD dedupe sane defaults; 3) consider alert aggregation threshold for synthetic checks.
Kai Chen: Agree. I’ll own the rollback and immediate mitigation. Meera will own the code fix. Brendan — can you own the alerting improvements? Sara — can you own PD incident hygiene (silences, update messaging)?
Meera Patel: Yep, will merge the dedupe PR after infra review and backport to prod prober image. Will also add a graceful fallback to accept cert chains with minor truncation for probes (non-production traffic only).
Sara L: I’ll prepare a short customer-impact note for AE/Sales: "No customer traffic was impacted; synthetic canaries misfired due to prober validation change; no action required by customers." Send to #customer-success for distribution.
Brendan M: Logged a temporary kanban card: INFRA-9245 for alert dedupe and INFRA-9246 for aggregation changes.
Kai Chen: Passing to Brendan in 45m for oncall handoff. Leaving note: rollback done, dedupe PR in staging, PD silenced.
Ops Rotation Bot: Oncall handoff: Brendan M is now primary oncall. Automated message.
Brendan M: ack. I’ll monitor for 30m and then start the post-incident writeup template. Any further spikes, re-open PD.
Meera Patel: Merged and deployed dedupe change to staging; scheduling prod roll after 1h dark-run. Will report status here.
Sara L: Closing the noisy PD silences in 25m if no further alerts. Drafting customer note now.
Kai Chen: Thanks all. Quick retrospective: we need canaries to be less chatty and PD dedupe must be stable across restarts. Lesson learned — synthetic tooling changes must land with rollout guard and smoke checks.
Brendan M: +1. Will file for blameless postmortem and link to this thread.
Incident Bot: Thread closed (auto) — incident resolved; final severity: P1 (no customer impact).
